EscalationGame

Escrows outcome REP, raises the running resolution cost, detects non-decision, and settles local or carried deposits. EscalationGame source contract

Read surface

Base getters are securityPool, repToken, activationTime, nonDecisionThresholdAttoRep, startBondAttoRep, nonDecisionTimestamp, nonDecisionState, forkContinuation, forkElapsedAtStart, forkResumedAt, fixedQuestionOutcome, nodes, disputeStakedRepByVaultAttoRep, totalDisputeStakedAttoRep, truthAuctionRepBeforeAttoRep, truthAuctionRepRemainingAttoRep, ordinarySettlementInitialized, ordinaryWinningReserveAttoRep, ordinarySettlementForkThresholdAttoRep, creditedSurplusAttoRep, and winnerHaircutPaidByFork. Ordinary settlement fixes the winner liability and threshold; losing local deposits and escrow read as zero afterward, while raw historical nodes remain stored. The fallback forwards every selector other than the two signed deposits to EscalationGameClaimDelegate, which provides the reads rootClaimSourceGame, getInheritedClaimAllocation, and getUnresolvedClaimInterval, plus getClaimCheckpointProgress, getClaimCheckpointState, getClaimCheckpointWitnessSegment, getReusableClaimCheckpoint, getClaimIntervalTransform, and isClaimHistoryFrozen. Standalone allocation reads inspect at most eight ancestors; deeper histories require permissionless checkpoint preparation. Central portfolio reporter claims keep identity coordinates across live branches and resolve their interval without ancestor traversal; their membership proofs and per-branch nullifiers still apply. getClaimCheckpointProgress distinguishes stored completion from readiness through the bounded read path. getClaimCheckpointState returns initialization, the pending commitment, the reused ancestor, and the current four-coordinate interval. getClaimCheckpointWitnessSegment returns the canonical source, prior commitment, first step, and length of the active segment; at most eight local transform reads reconstruct the batch from current state. getReusableClaimCheckpoint exports a completed interval and its excluded immediate-source anchor; descendants select caches only along their canonical lineage for the same claim tuple. The allocation read returns source principal, retained principal, reward-interval length, and the cumulative reward endpoint after per-generation auction rounding. The reward interval is the deposit’s range within its outcome’s cumulative deposits: its start is the returned endpoint minus the returned length. It determines which portion enters the reward calculation; the length is not a payable reward. Exported principal intervals compact consumed prefixes, while reward positions remain unshifted by prior claims. Allocations within a game stay fixed in every claim order. disputeStakedRepByVaultAttoRep is nominal reporter principal, not collateral value. getDisputeBackingAttoRep returns actual game REP; getVaultDisputeBackingAttoRep credits ordinary reports only for their contribution retained after source surplus, and returns zero for continuation claims. Inherited carry remains aggregate commitment state until proof settlement. Use previewDepositOnOutcome, computeIterativeAttritionCostAttoRep, computeTimeSinceStartFromAttritionCostAttoRep, totalCostAttoRep, getEscalationGameEndDate, getQuestionResolution, getFinalQuestionResolution, hasReachedNonDecision, canTriggerOwnFork, getBindingCapitalAttoRep, getOutcomeBalancesAttoRep, getDepositsByOutcome, getDepositsByOutcomeLength, forkCarrySnapshotInitialized, forkCarrySnapshotOutcomesInitialized, getOutcomeState, getForkCarrySnapshot, getForkCarryRoots, isForkCarryFundingComplete, getCarryLeafPageByOutcome, getProofConsumedCarriedDepositIndexesByOutcome, getLocalUnresolvedPrincipalByVaultAndOutcome, and getForkedEscrowByVaultAndOutcome for calculations, lifecycle authorization, pages, carry state, and escrow. getCarryLeafPageByOutcome limits visited nodes by maxEntries, including consumed nodes; empty or short pages may return a nonzero continuation cursor. Vault-funded deposits and ordinary withdrawals route through SecurityPool, while own-fork direct claims route through SecurityPoolForker; after an ordinary game starts, wallet-funded deposits use depositRepOnOutcome, depositRepOnOutcomeWithPermit, or depositRepOnOutcomeWithAuthorization and mint no pool backing units.

State-changing interactions

Each call lists its parameter names in ABI order. The contract index defines the columns. Rows marked "through fallback()" are not in the compiled ABI: the fallback forwards the two signed deposit selectors to EscalationGameDepositDelegate and every other unknown selector to EscalationGameClaimDelegate by delegatecall, and returns or reverts with the delegate output. A call restricted to the owning pool or its forker reverts without reason data for any other caller. For central portfolio custody, report REP is held in the reporter ledger, independently of provider REP. Unrelated resumed continuations accept wallet-funded deposits. Fixed-outcome continuations end exactly three days after the child response anchor, which is the native parent fork time plus nine weeks; late materialization does not extend it. Other continuation deadlines retain their inherited elapsed time and minimum response period. A later native fork interrupts unresolved reporting before any fixed outcome can be returned. Native per-question REP exports and Truth Auction haircuts reject central custody.

Initializes a local game and sets activation three days after deployment. For ordinary pool games, the factory lowers an oversized configured bond to nonDecisionThresholdAttoRep - 1 before this call. All three carry outcomes must be initialized (Fork snapshot incomplete), even for empty history. When the canonical factory records nonzero initial backing, the live reporter balance must cover that actual escrow after source surplus and native fork burn, minus valid direct pre-resume exports and scaled by any applyTruthAuctionHaircut. Without recorded initial backing, it must cover effective inherited unresolved principal plus local unresolved principal across all three outcomes. Resumes once carry funding is complete. Bound continuations use the fixed portfolio response anchor; when their outcome is fixed, the deadline is exactly anchor plus three days, otherwise inherited attrition and the minimum response interval apply. Late materialization never moves the anchor. Final resolution also checks whether the native universe forked before that deadline. ForkContinuationResumed

Settles one local deposit after resolution. An ordinary first claim freezes the winning liability and burns terminal excess beyond the surplus already paid at source; ordinary losers retire together and a valid losing index returns zero repeatedly. A winner consumes its reserved payout and burn and pays the immutable depositor. Continuation losers still consume their individual escrow. OrdinarySettlementInitialized on first ordinary settlement. Retired ordinary losers emit no per-deposit settlement event.

The nonzero full snapshot identity and source are fixed on the first call. The third call verifies the installed data against that identity before marking the snapshot complete. processClaimCheckpoint(outcomeIndex, amountAttoRep, cumulativeAmountAttoRep, leafIndex, maxSteps, baseCommitment, transforms) through fallback() Anyone Complete fork snapshot when applicable; valid outcome and interval; maxSteps from 1 to 8 and no more transforms than that budget (Invalid checkpoint budget). An empty transform array requires a zero base commitment (Invalid checkpoint base). Discovery requires empty transforms (Checkpoint discovery pending) and each committed source to be PoolForked with its migration window closed. Applying queued transforms requires a nonempty batch no longer than the pending step count (Checkpoint transforms required), whose forward hash matches the pending commitment bound to this game and claim tuple (Invalid checkpoint batch); invalid or stale batches revert atomically. Completed calls and successful parent-cache adoption do not apply supplied transforms. Claims still require authenticated membership and an unspent nullifier. An empty transform array with a zero base commitment discovers at most eight frozen ancestor transforms per call and commits them to a hash stack. A completed canonical ancestor checkpoint for the same claim tuple replaces its already-prepared prefix; the excluded source transform is still processed. After discovery, a batch supplies one base commitment and at most eight transforms in forward hash order. The complete batch must hash to the pending commitment before those transforms apply in reverse order, preserving every generation’s integer rounding. Each transform contains repBeforeAttoRep, repRemainingAttoRep, and consumedBeforeAttoRep. Recovery anchors store a source and prior hash for each eight-transform segment. Every unfinished call checks the immediate parent’s completed cache; if available, it replaces even partially applied preparation with that prefix plus its one frozen excluded-source transform. Otherwise initialization reads the immediate source. The target and immediate parent remain live reads. Preparation does not consume a proof or move REP; completed calls are idempotent. ClaimCheckpointProgress; returns whether the stored checkpoint is complete. Read getClaimCheckpointProgress for readiness and remaining traversal state

The game runs the same step internally while installing a carry snapshot with a nonzero source game, and no pool function calls this selector. No event

settleOrdinaryGame() Anyone Ordinary game, not a fork continuation, with nonDecisionState = None and a final outcome. Game REP must cover the initial winner reserve (Winner reserve underfunded). Freezes the final outcome and effective fork threshold, reserves the cumulative winning payout and burn liability, and retires all losing local escrow without visiting deposits. Each later winning claim subtracts its payout and burn from that reserve. Burns terminal REP above the reserve; the ordinary minimum-outcome surplus was already paid irrevocably as deposits arrived. A repeated call with no surplus succeeds. Native final backing redemption calls this before valuing units. See ESC-11. OrdinarySettlementInitialized once; OrdinaryResidualRepBurned and REP Transfer only when surplus is positive

Continuations require no effective unresolved principal and, after retiring inherited aggregate escrow, no remaining local stake or vault escrow. Applies ordinary winner-reserve settlement and burns its terminal excess. Also burns fork-continuation residual so pre-child capital cannot accrue to late or nonexistent child owners. OrdinarySettlementInitialized if first ordinary settlement, then OrdinaryResidualRepBurned; ForkContinuationResidualRepBurned for a fork continuation

Accounting examples

Required support threshold

The contract waits ACTIVATION_DELAY (3 days) after start() before the escalation clock begins. From day 3 the cumulative binding-capital requirement rises from the configured start bond S to the non-decision threshold T over the 49-day ESCALATION_TIME_LENGTH, reaching T on day 52. The contract evaluates a fixed-point curve; this expression is its readable idealization.

A(d)=0for0≤d≤3=S×exp(ln(TS)×d−349)for3<d<52=Tford≥52

Winning-deposit payout

Binding capital is the median outcome balance at settlement; no outcome balance can exceed the non-decision threshold. The reward-eligible cap is binding capital plus binding capital divided by EXCESS_REWARD_WINDOW_DIVISOR (2), so only the portion of winning deposits up to 1.5 × binding capital participates in the bonus. Of the binding capital, 3 / 5 funds the reward pool and 2 / 5 funds the escalation-haircut pool; both are shared pro rata across the reward-eligible principal, which is the smaller of the winning outcome balance and that cap.

Let binding capital be 10 REP, so the reward-eligible cap is 15 REP, the reward pool is 6 REP, and the escalation-haircut pool is 4 REP. If the winning outcome holds 15 REP and one deposit contributed 5 REP inside the eligible range:

  • Principal returned: 5 REP.
  • Bonus: 5 × 6 / 15 = 2 REP.
  • Winning payout: 5 + 2 = 7 REP.
  • Haircut burned: 5 × 4 / 15 = 1.333333333333333333 REP at attoREP precision.

A winning deposit position above 15 REP returns its principal without a bonus. When Zoltar's fork threshold at settlement is below the game's non-decision threshold, the whole withdrawal is scaled by their ratio. If this game's non-decision threshold were 20 REP and the fork threshold 16 REP, the 7 REP payout becomes 7 × 16 / 20 = 5.6 REP, rounded down to attoREP. Fork scaling can therefore reduce the final transfer below principal.
